senses.gloss: m. (θρόνος) chair, throne. Tanḥ. T’rumah 9 עד שלא … על ת׳ של וכ׳ (some ed. ט׳, corr. acc.) so long as the Temple was not built, the world rested on a throne of two legs; when the Temple was built, the world stood firm (v. בָּסַס); Y’lamd. ib., quot. in Ar. תרנוס; Tanḥ. ed. Bub. ib. 8 תרנוס (Var. תרכוס; corr. acc.).
units: <cite ref="Bereishit Rabbah 68">Gen. R. s. 68</cite> <he>ת׳ של שלש וכ׳</he> (not <cite ref="V01010"><he>תרכוסא</he></cite>) he showed him (Jacob) a throne on three legs (the three pillars of the world); <cite ref="Yalkut Shimoni on Torah 119:4">Yalk. ib. 119</cite> <cite ref="V01025"><he>תרנוס</he></cite>.

<cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Shabbat 3:7:8">Y. Sabb. III, 6ᶜ</cite> bot. <he>ת׳ אסור וכ׳</he> (ed. <cite ref="V01009"><he>תרכוס</he></cite>, corr. acc.) it is forbidden to move a large (teacher’s) chair (on the Sabbath, interch. with <he>כסא</he>); a. e.—[Gen. R. l. c. <he>כמטה וכת׳</he> Ar. (ed. <he>וכפרנוס</he>; Yalk. l. c. <he>וכפורנס</he>) read: <he>וכטורוס</he>, v. <cite ref="I00220"><he>טוֹרוּס</he></cite>, a. <cite ref="Q00976"><he>פְּלוּמָא</he></cite>.]
